title: DRAW: the outcome a0-111 could not produce, asked for again
sub: Production bundle built from origin/main @ e498b831, ?debug=1, no ?freeze (so the build stamp e498b83* is legible in the corner of every frame). Every core is brought down through the sim's own damage function on the ?debug=1 queue; nothing about the end screen's WORDS is staged, and there is still no draw seam to stage them with.

blocks.caption: LEFT: a0-111's frame (evidence/a0-111-yesterday-with-eyes/shots/desktop-1280x800-end-draw.png). RIGHT: this run (desktop-1280x800-draw-eight-at-once.png). Same rectangle x230 y450 w810 h310 of the same profile, 2x nearest-neighbour, no filtering. Left reads DEFEAT, a blue rule, then 'Player 8 won.' Right reads DRAW and then 'No reactor survived the collapse.' Both say MATCH TIME . 00:10: the same experiment, eight cores brought to 0 in a single simultaneous burst.

desktop 1280x800, experiment A - a0-111's burst reproduced exactly: one lethal damageCore(p, 999) queued for all EIGHT seats in a single call. Headline DRAW. Under it 'No reactor survived the collapse.' and 'MATCH TIME . 00:10'. Buttons REMATCH and BACK TO MENU. No line anywhere names a player and no line says anyone won. Stamp e498b83* bottom left.

desktop 1280x800, experiment B - the case a real match produces: seats 7,6,5,4,3,2 killed one at a time (the match keeps running), leaving the local player seat 0 and rival seat 1 on 100 HP each, then those two killed in a single call so they fall on the same tick. Same words: DRAW / 'No reactor survived the collapse.' MATCH TIME . 00:15, +135 XP.
phone landscape 798x384, experiment B. DRAW / 'No reactor survived the collapse.' The headline and its line survive the narrowest supported width without wrapping or clipping.

title: The refused HOST: where RETRY and DOWNLOAD LOG land now
sub: Production bundle @ e498b831, ?gate=0 - the front door, walked: PLAY, then a REAL press at the HOST door's own reported centre, with no allocator on this box to reach. The refusal is real, not staged.

blocks.caption: LEFT: a0-111's frame (a0-111-yesterday-with-eyes/shots/phone-798x384-join-3-host.png). RIGHT: this run (phone-798x384-host-1-refused.png). Same rectangle x620 y190 w660 h320, 2x. On the left the DOWNLOAD LOG button is drawn ON the HOST plate: only the top edges of H-O-S-T show under it and the word cannot be read. On the right DOWNLOAD LOG sits above the plate and HOST reads in full.

phone 798x384, the whole frame. Red 'FAILED: no allocator configured', then 'DOWNLOAD LOG to report this.', then the RETRY and DOWNLOAD LOG buttons - all three above the door grid. CAMPAIGN, SOLO, HOST and JOIN are each fully legible, name and subtitle. Measured: the buttons occupy y127.4-171.4 and the topmost door starts at y186.4, ~15px clear. Build stamp e498b83* bottom left, where it clips the left edge of the BACK plate - that is the debug badge this brief deliberately keeps visible, not a layout defect.

desktop 1280x800, the same route. Buttons at y217.4-261.4, topmost door (CAMPAIGN) at y314.2: ~53px clear. HOST reads in full. elementFromPoint at all five doors' own reported centres returns the canvas, so nothing intercepts a door's press.

title: The ore counter: fourteen stops per profile, measured the way a0-111 measured it
sub: Production bundle @ e498b831, ?debug=1. a0-111's measurement untouched: the same fourteen headings in the same order, reached by the same real taps, with every other registered element's rect intersected against the counter's own rect at every stop. __oreHudStage.mine(37) puts ore in the hold; where the counter is drawn and what lands in it is the HUD's business.

blocks.caption: Desktop stop 7, the frame a0-111's verdict was written from. LEFT: a0-111. RIGHT: this run. Same rectangle x20 y30 w290 h130, 4x. On the left the teal 'Rusty (EASY)' is drawn across the counter - its R sits on the E of ORE. On the right ORE and the numeral 3 are clean: the label has stepped sideways, clear of the counter's rect.

desktop stop 0, a0-111's other real collision. ORE and 3 in the top-left corner with nothing drawn into them; 'Rusty (EASY)' stands to the right of the counter, over the station. Nothing is drawn over the word ORE or the numeral.

desktop stop 12 - the ONE stop of fourteen that still reports a non-empty intersection this run. Nothing is visible in the counter: ORE and 3 are clean. The reported overlap is the nameplates LAYER's union rect (x59.3 y31.8 w284.2 h626.9, the bounding box of two plates 'YOU' and 'Rusty' far apart) clipping the counter's corner by 9.5x59.2, with neither glyph near it. a0-111's frame at this same stop reports a numerically identical overlap and is likewise clean.

title: The alarm arrow and the wave clock: is WAVE readable now
sub: Production bundle @ e498b831 - which INCLUDES a0-116 (PR #493, merged as 6c9963c2). ?debug=1, no ?freeze. Staging is a0-111's: __oreHudStage.mine(0) puts home off screen, plus a held siege (damageCore(0, 2) every 400ms above a 30 HP floor) because the alarm latches 5s and drains, and a leisurely dpr-2 capture otherwise photographs a released alarm. The wave clock has no layout-registry row, so there is no intersection number for it and none is invented: the verdict is read off the magnified crop, which is the instrument a0-111 used.

blocks.caption: phone 798x384, top-centre band, rectangle x500 y0 w600 h220 at 3x on all three panels. LEFT: a0-111's frame - the red arrow is drawn on the clock's first line and covers the A of WAVE; the line reads 'W VE 1/5 . Outer Drift'. MIDDLE: this run at a0-111's own bearing - the arrow has dropped below the clock's hairline rule and WAVE 1/5 . Outer Drift reads in full. RIGHT: this run at the worst bearing eight real taps could find (sweep stop 1), where the arrow's centre stands 1.8 logical px from the horizontal centre of the glass - dead centre of the top edge - and it is still below the rule, with all three lines WAVE 1/5 . Outer Drift, NEXT 2:04 and MATCH 0:27 readable.

desktop 1280x800, rectangle x850 y0 w900 h200 at 3x. LEFT a0-111: the arrow sits on the clock's first line, immediately against the W of WAVE. RIGHT this run: the arrow is below the hairline rule under MATCH, clear of all three lines. Its registry rect moved from y13.9 (a0-111) to y85.0 - it gave up radius, not bearing.

phone 798x384, sweep stop 1, the whole frame. The red arrow points straight up from below the wave clock; the under-attack prompt 'Your station is under attack - follow the arrow' is drawn at the bottom; the pulsing red alarm frame is up around the glass. Stamp e498b83* bottom left.

title: Not one of the four: two nameplates drawn on each other
sub: Seen while sampling the ore counter (item 3), on the production bundle @ e498b831. Reported here because it is visible in a committed frame, not because it was looked for.

blocks.caption: desktop ore stop 7, rectangle x120 y55 w620 h80 at 4x. Two teal nameplates are drawn overlapping: the strip reads 'Rusty(ERusty(EASY)'. __nameplateStage.plates() reports two plates at this stop, both owner 1, both text 'Rusty'. In the overlap neither label can be read. A health bar 42/70 sits under them. This is a legibility fault between two world labels, NOT a label in a HUD readout - the ore counter itself is clean in this frame.
The whole frame it was cut from. The counter (ORE / 3) is clean in the top-left; the doubled label sits to its right, over the station.
